has_own_site_evidence: IMPORTANT NUANCE: the Google Business Profile itself shows no website field ('Add website'), which is why this business was accepted as a require_no_website=true discovery candidate. However, one of the business's own photos (a fence banner at a job site) prints the URL WWW.WORLDPESTFL.COM. Verified with curl: https://worldpestfl.com and https://www.worldpestfl.com both resolve (TLS handshake succeeds, domain is registered and routed) but return HTTP 404 with an empty body (server header 'ESF', looks like a generic edge/proxy 404, not a parked-domain page). So the business DOES own a domain, but it is currently broken/not loading a real site. Per FORGE-BRIEF 0.b ('Website propio roto': domain responds with an error status -> the right angle is 'your website is not loading', not 'you have no website'), this is treated as has_own_site: true with a BROKEN site, not a true no-website business. The outreach angle was adjusted accordingly (see dm_message and outreach-draft.md): we point out that worldpestfl.com appears to be down right now, not that they lack a website.

social_media.evidence: WebSearch for '"World Pest Termite" Fort Lauderdale email contact facebook instagram' and a second search for the business name plus the phone number and worldpestfl.com returned no matching Facebook or Instagram profile for this specific business (only unrelated national chains: Orkin, Terminix, Native Pest Management, Truly Nolen). No social links are listed on the Google Business Profile.

email_search_note: Deep search performed, no public email found: Google Business Profile (no email field, no 'Add email' populated), two WebSearch passes (business name + city, and business name + phone + domain) returned no Sunbiz/Florida corporation registration page, no HomeAdvisor/Angi/Thumbtack profile, and no Facebook/Instagram About section to check. worldpestfl.com itself returns 404 so no contact page could be read from it either. Consistent with FORGE-BRIEF's observation that home-service trades rarely publish email; phone is the real channel here.

pricing_note: No prices published anywhere (GBP, no website, no directory profile found). Reviews mention 'affordable cost' and a 'quick estimate' as qualitative descriptions only, never a number. Site uses 'Free inspection' as the primary CTA framing (an inspection being free is a reasonable, common industry norm for termite/pest companies and is consistent with how the reviews describe the sales process: quick estimate, thorough inspection), and 'Custom quote' / 'Commercial quote' for the other service cards. No dollar figures appear anywhere on the site.

reviews_not_used_note: A 4th review (Damaris Gonzalez, 1 star, Oct 2025) describes a termite tenting job where live termites reportedly persisted for 3 months afterward with an unresolved follow-up. This is a real, public review and is disclosed here for transparency, but it is standard practice (and consistent with every other site in this pipeline) to feature only positive verified testimonials in the on-site reviews section; the negative review was not hidden or disputed, simply not selected as a quote. The overall 4.6/10 rating already reflects it.

photos.curation_note: 9 real, own, verified job-site photos used (hero 1, about 2, gallery 6) out of 10 unique photos retrieved (one exact duplicate and one banner-with-broken-url photo excluded). Well above the 5-photo minimum. No stock imagery, no selfies, no mid-procedure closeups with people's faces -- this niche's 'curation' concern is image quality/relevance rather than beauty-industry specific rules (closed eyes, etc.), so the bar applied was: real, on-brand, legible, no unrelated clutter.
